title: Old pending city assembly failure can be attributed to a newer rejected preparation
earliest_failed_contract: Pending city product lacks its own PreparationTicket; asynchronous publish_candidate borrows whichever ticket is currently stored in independent last-installation status.
counterexample: A accepted replacement retains pendingA and status(A,Preparing). Before A assembly publishes, install B is rejected, for example malformed document JSON; install sets status(B,Failed,Input) and intentionally retains pendingA. If A subsequently receives actual CityAssemblyFailure, publish_candidate removes A but replaces status with failed(status.preparation,Assembly), producing B/Assembly although B never entered assembly.
actual_recipient: regional_map/status.rs168 serializes this city_installation record into STATUS JSON, served by json180-185. Wrong preparation/error pairing is externally observable report data.
qualification: Conditional API/async ordering; current code permits both calls and actual assemblyfailure path exists. No ordinary browser sends this sequence, bad live city, observed report or executed reproduction claimed. Keeping a last-good installed or older pending product is legitimate policy; its failure must retain its own identity. General phase/error neighbor aggregate risk in ROOT-OWNER-CITY-SURFACE-048 is related evidence, not this exact causal attribution proof.
connected_repair: Bind each pending candidate to exact ticket and publish outcomes against that candidate identity. Define latest-attempt report versus still-pending product status explicitly, so late A completion/failure cannot rewrite B cause. Preserve transactional candidate replacement, last-good installed visibility, cleanup and stale candidate ownership.
acceptance: After A pending then B rejects, A assemblyfailure cannot relabel B Input as Assembly or use Bticket for Aoutcome. Successful replacement and pointer-resident idempotency preserve exactticket/status semantics. No tests added or executed.
